home.title: andarama | ¡anda! open source 360 virtual tours
home.description: ¡anda! andarama lets me walk through panoramas. Create, publish and share 360 virtual tours with a visual editor, a WebGL viewer with VR, quizzes, SCORM and open export. Open source (EUPL-1.2): free on your own server, hosted from $2 a month.
home.og_description: andarama lets me walk through panoramas. Upload your 360 photos, connect them like you would sketch a floor plan and publish a tour anyone can stroll through from any browser, headset included.
home.og_alt: “¡anda!” in huge letters on bone-coloured paper, with three yellow creatures walking along a line

portada.explica: Upload your 360 photos, connect them like you would sketch a floor plan and publish a tour anyone can stroll through from any browser, VR headset included.
portada.susurro: open source (EUPL-1.2) · free on your own server · hosted here from $2 a month

lista.texto: From any 360 camera or from your phone. The importer reads a whole batch, sorts by the camera's numbering, renames by pattern and tiles the panoramas in your own browser, up to 32K, without waiting for any server.
Drag one scene onto another and there is a step, with its way back. In the graph every arrow is a navigation hotspot: there is no parallel data to drift out of sync.
Text, photos, videos, audio, PDFs, 3D models, questions, forms, floor plans, narration with spatial audio and translations. Eighteen hotspot types, every one of them usable inside the headset too.
A link, an iframe, your own domain or a ZIP that works on any hosting. Kiosk mode for a TV screen, SCORM for Moodle, PWA to view it offline.

editor.titulo: You edit by looking, not by filling in forms
editor.p1: The preview is the real viewer in edit mode: what you see is what gets published. Click on the photo to place a hotspot, drag to move it, draw a polygon vertex by vertex.
editor.p2: The orientation you arrive with in a room belongs to the path, not to the room: entering the living room from the hallway and from the kitchen are two different arrivals, and each one keeps its own view. The “How you get here” panel gathers them all where they can be judged: in the destination scene.
tics: Unlimited undo and redo, autosave with a warning if something fails to reach the server
Version history with per-scene and per-hotspot diffs, and restore
Command palette, keyboard shortcuts and a tabbed properties panel
Presence and soft per-scene locking when several of you edit, anchored comments with threads
Side-by-side translations with completion percentage, XLIFF and CSV
editor.alt: The Andarama editor showing a scene from Geisenheim cathedral, the scene list on the left and the arrivals panel on the right

grafo.titulo: The map of the tour, drawn
grafo.p1: A canvas with thumbnails, ports, marquee selection, minimap and auto-layout. You connect by dragging from the edge of a node and the way back is created at once. It warns about steps without a destination, without a way back, not yet placed, and about scenes nobody can reach.
grafo.p2: In Autopilot mode the same canvas draws guided tours: stops with dwell time, entry through the step that joins the two scenes and a turn towards the exit before crossing. It is what the kiosk and the auto-tour button play back.
grafo.alt: The tour graph with scenes grouped by area and connections drawn as arrows

tablero.titulo: Everything within reach, like on a desk
tablero.p1: Folders, tags, templates, a thirty-day bin and search. The cover of each tour is the panorama of its starting scene. Duplicate, rename, share with a colleague and their role.
tablero.p2: The library shows a little planet when you hover over any panorama, computed locally without touching the network, and a double click opens the photo in 360 so you can check it before using it. A single file, a selection or a whole folder can be dragged onto the graph and out come scenes.
tics: Direct multipart, resumable uploads, no duplicates thanks to content hashing
GPano and EXIF metadata with GPS, levelling and nadir adjustment without destroying the original
Cascading defaults: instance, organisation, user, template and tour
tablero.alt: The Andarama projects dashboard with the covers of four tours

hotspots.titulo: Eighteen ways to touch the photo
hotspots.texto: Every hotspot has a position, an icon, a label, distance scaling and conditions (language, variables, video timestamp). And they all show up in the headset as pictograms you touch with your hand.

Any phone without WebXR: split screen, gyroscope orientation with the iOS permission, gaze selection with a dwell ring and the physical button of cardboard goggles.

With a gyroscope, a reticle appears that opens whatever you look at. Immersive panels are drawn inside the session: text, image, gallery, video with transport, audio with transcript, scored quiz and comparer with a divider.

nube.texto: No Andarama module talks directly to Cloudflare: everything goes through an adapter layer. That is why self-hosting is not a cut-down version but the very same application.

lista.texto: Workers, D1, R2, KV, Durable Objects and Analytics Engine, within the free tier for small and medium use. pnpm deploy:cloudflare and in ten minutes there is an instance.

A single file for macOS, Windows and Linux with the server, the Studio and the viewer inside. Double click, the browser opens and the data stays in your home folder. No Docker, no Node, no account with anyone.
Node and SQLite in a single image, one volume and one port. docker compose up -d. Backups with a script and the portable .andarama file.
CSP with nonces, HSTS, secure sessions, double-token CSRF, rate limits, Turnstile, sanitised SVG, Markdown and CSS, audit log and permissions checked on the server on every route.

Organisations with roles (admin, editor, contributor, reader), per-project sharing, invitations, two-step verification and an admin panel with quotas and usage. On a self-hosted install, institutional SSO via OIDC with automatic sign-up by domain as well.

Full keyboard, visible focus, 44-pixel targets, scene-change announcements, per-scene alt text with a reviewable AI suggestion (the editor warns if it is missing), prefers-reduced-motion, WebVTT subtitles and translations per scene and per hotspot. We are working towards WCAG 2.1 AA: the actual status is in the accessibility statement.

EUPL-1.2, strict TypeScript across the monorepo, hundreds of unit and end-to-end tests, continuous integration with dependency audits. The tour.json format guarantees that what you export will keep opening. Code, issues and downloads are at github.com/joseluissaorin/andarama.

nube.susurro: on andarama.com accounts and payments are handled by Clerk · the data stays in Andarama's own database

nombre.p1: Panorama was coined in 1791 to name “the view of everything”. Since then the suffix -rama has served for ways of looking: diorama, cyclorama, cinerama.
nombre.p2: We only changed the verb. Andar is Spanish for “to walk”: a panorama is something you look at, an andarama is something you walk through.
nombre.susurro: from “andar” + “-rama” · and yes, the yellow creature walks too

lista.q: Where is the code?
lista.a: On GitHub, under EUPL-1.2. You can read it, install it, modify it and contribute. Desktop executables and release notes are published in the releases of the same repository.

lista.q: Which camera do I need?
lista.a: Any that produces an equirectangular photo (Insta360, Ricoh Theta, GoPro Max, Kandao…) or a phone with a panorama app. Cubemaps, partial panoramas and gigapixel flat photos work too. Tiling happens in your browser up to 32K; above that, on the server.

lista.q: Do the tours keep working if Andarama disappears?
lista.a: Yes. The exported ZIP is static and self-contained: HTML, the viewer and the tiles. Upload it to any hosting, open it from a USB stick with the single HTML file, and it keeps virtual reality. And the tour.json format is documented and versioned.

lista.q: Where does my data live?
lista.a: If you self-host, on your server or in your Cloudflare account. On andarama.com, in Andarama's database; Clerk only stores the account and the billing. Visitor analytics use no cookies and store no IP addresses.

lista.q: Does it work with Moodle?
lista.a: Yes, with the SCORM 1.2 or 2004 package: upload it to Moodle (or Canvas, Blackboard, Sakai…) like any other activity and it reports completion and the quiz grade. The LTI 1.3 integration is in testing and we enable it on request.

lista.q: Can I work with other people on the same tour?
lista.a: Yes. Organisations with roles, per-project sharing, presence and soft per-scene locking so you don't step on each other, comments anchored on the photo and version history to go back.

lista.q: Which headsets work?
lista.a: Any with a WebXR browser (Meta Quest, Pico, Vision Pro with Safari, a PC with a headset). Open the tour's address from the headset's browser and press the VR button. Without a headset, cardboard mode works on any phone.

lista.q: What does “fair use” mean?
lista.a: That the plans are meant for one person or a small team. If usage stops looking like that, we talk before cutting anything off. And if you need something without quotas, self-hosting is free and it is the same program.

precios.texto: Andarama is open source: free if you install it yourself. If you would rather have us look after it, andarama.com offers six plans. All of them have project limits and a fair-use policy.
precios.prueba: 14-day free trial, no card required; then from $20/month.

museos.title: Museum virtual tour software for museums, archives and heritage | andarama
museos.description: Museum virtual tour in 360 with labels, audio guide, PDFs and 3D models, live guided tours for schools, quizzes, accessibility and free export. Open source, GDPR.
museos.h1: Museum virtual tour: 360 tours for museums, archives and heritage sites
museos.lead: A 360 tour through the galleries, the stacks or the monument, with the labels, the audio guide and the works in high resolution anchored right where they are. For museums, archives, libraries, heritage bodies and local councils. Open source, GDPR-compliant, and a tour that belongs to the museum, not to the platform.

usos.texto: Any institution that looks after a place and wants to show it to those who cannot come, or to prepare the visit for those who can.
lista: Museums and art centres: the galleries, the temporary exhibition that is about to close and the storerooms that never open to the public.
Archives and libraries: closed stacks, gigapixel documents with map-style zoom and complete PDFs anchored on the shelf.
Heritage and monuments: churches, castles, archaeological sites and buildings under restoration or with limited capacity.
Councils, city halls and regional governments: a territory's whole network of museums and monuments, with its own page per place and accounts per department.

bloques.titulo: A navigable virtual tour, with the information where it belongs
bloques.texto: 360 photos of every room linked by navigation steps, a floor plan per level to find your way and a scene menu by area. Next to each piece, a hotspot with the label as text, the audio guide, the work in high resolution with zoom, the catalogue as PDF or the 3D model in glTF, which on a phone also opens in augmented reality. And in your visitors' languages: every scene and every hotspot is translated inside the editor itself.

bloques.titulo: Live guided tour for school groups
bloques.texto: The educator creates a room with a code and shares the link: the whole class sees the scene and the viewing angle they set, they point with the pointer and write in the chat; each pupil can break away to look around on their own and sync back up. Voice goes over whatever video call the school already uses. Nothing to install: from the browser, on the interactive whiteboard or on tablets.

bloques.titulo: Quiz and treasure hunt for young visitors
bloques.texto: Questions scattered through the galleries, with feedback, points and a gate that keeps the visitor in the scene until they get it right. Hidden objects with the Treasure hotspot and a visible count of those found. State variables that open a door once everything has been found. And at the end, a report and a PDF certificate with the participant's name. Schools can build the same thing on the Aula plan.

Every scene can carry alternative text (the editor warns if it is missing) and the viewer offers a linear accessible-content mode: the whole tour reads as text, with a screen reader or without a mouse. WebVTT subtitles for 360 video and video hotspots, visible focus, 44 px touch targets and prefers-reduced-motion respected. We are working towards WCAG 2.1 AA; what is already met and what is not is set out in the accessibility statement.

bloques.titulo: The tour belongs to the museum: free export
bloques.texto: One click exports a static, self-contained ZIP (HTML, viewer, tour.json, tiles and media) that runs on any server with no Andarama behind it. Also as a single HTML file, as a PWA that works offline or in kiosk mode for the lobby screen, with autopilot and reset after inactivity. The format is documented: if the museum stops using Andarama, it takes the whole tour with it.

A public tour on the hosted instance can request its own page in the public gallery: a title with the name of the place, description, country and coordinates, structured place data and an entry in the sitemap. A URL that search engines find by the museum's name and that leads to its website. The index is filtered by country.

Visitor analytics use no cookies and store no IP addresses: they give visits, time per room and where people look without tracking anyone. The program is open source under EUPL-1.2, the European Commission's licence: it can be read, audited and installed on the infrastructure of the museum or of the authority it belongs to.

bloques.titulo: Your own instance with support, or the Formación plan
bloques.texto: Two ways. The hosted Formación plan on andarama.com: up to 100 tours, 200 GB, no badge, your own domain, a team and an invoice in euros on request with the institution's tax details. Or the very same application deployed on the museum's Cloudflare or Docker, with support, updates and onboarding for staff. The terms for institutions are on the universities page.

faq.titulo: Frequently asked questions about museum virtual tours

lista.q: What does it take to make a virtual tour of a museum?
lista.a: 360 photos of the rooms, from any camera that produces an equirectangular image or from a phone; the texts, audio and images the museum already has; and an afternoon in the editor to link it all together. Photography sets the cost: the software can be free, installed on your own server, or whichever plan fits. The line items, with figures, are in Museum virtual tour: how it is made and what it costs.

lista.q: Can it run on a screen inside the museum?
lista.a: Yes. Kiosk mode walks through the rooms on its own, lets any visitor take control and returns to the start after a while without activity, with exit locked. And the PWA package works offline, so the lobby screen does not depend on the network.

lista.q: How do you run a guided tour with a school?
lista.a: The educator publishes the tour, creates a room from the editor and shares the attendee link. Everything they do (changing room, turning the view, zooming) is mirrored on the class's screens; they point with the pointer and answer in the chat. Voice goes over the video call the school already uses. Rooms are ephemeral: they vanish when the guide leaves.

lista.q: Does it work for an archive or a library?
lista.a: Yes. Besides 360 scenes there are 2D gigapixel scenes to explore a digitised document or artwork with map-style zoom and annotations anchored on the page itself, plus PDF hotspots with a built-in viewer. We walk through it step by step in A 360 tour for an archive or a library.

lista.q: What if the museum stops using Andarama?
lista.a: It takes the whole tour with it. The exported ZIP is static and self-contained: HTML, viewer, tour.json, tiles and media. Upload it by FTP to any hosting, to GitHub Pages or to Cloudflare Pages and it keeps working with no platform behind it. The format is documented and the program is open source under EUPL-1.2.

lista.q: Is it GDPR-compliant?
lista.a: Yes. Visitor analytics use no cookies and store no IP addresses; the session identifier is ephemeral and the data is aggregated. Data lives wherever the institution says: on its server, in its Cloudflare account or on andarama.com, with a data-processing agreement we prepare on request.

lista.q: Can it be viewed with a VR headset?
lista.a: The same tour opens on Meta Quest, Pico or Vision Pro straight from their browser, with the text panels, audio and quiz inside the session. And in cardboard mode on any phone, which is what a classroom usually has.

wordpress.title: WordPress plugin for 360 virtual tours | andarama
wordpress.description: The Andarama 360 plugin embeds virtual tours in WordPress with a block, a shortcode or by pasting the tour's URL. Open source and free.
wordpress.h1: 360 tours in WordPress, with a block
wordpress.lead: The Andarama 360 plugin drops the viewer into any post or page: paste the tour's address and you are done. Works with the block editor, the classic editor and page builders.

bloques.texto: An “Andarama 360 Tour” block with a live preview in the editor, the address pasted into an empty paragraph (like a YouTube video) or the [andarama url="…"] shortcode for Elementor, Divi, WPBakery and friends.
WebGL 360 panorama with gyroscope on phones, VR mode with WebXR, fullscreen, lazy loading and a choice of aspect ratio. The iframe ships with the permissions it needs.
In the plugin settings you enter the address of your Andarama instance, whether andarama.com or your own server. The plugin is free software (GPLv2 or later).

instalacion.titulo: Install it manually with the ZIP
instalacion.texto: The plugin is under review for the wordpress.org directory. In the meantime you install it by uploading the ZIP, which is the same file:
pasos: Download andarama-360.zip and do not unzip it.
In the WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins, click Add New Plugin and then Upload Plugin.
Choose the ZIP, click Install Now and, once it finishes, Activate.
In the plugin settings, check your instance address (andarama.com is preset) and the default aspect ratio.
Edit a post, add the “Andarama 360 Tour” block or paste the tour's address into an empty paragraph.
instalacion.sin_plugin: Can't install plugins? It works without one too: paste the iframe or the script line you get from the “Embed” button when you publish. The embedding guide explains how.

privacidad.title: Privacy and cookie policy | andarama
privacidad.description: What data andarama.com processes, with which providers (Cloudflare, Clerk, Plausible, email), which cookies it uses and what happens if you arrive from an ad.
privacidad.lead: This page explains what data andarama.com processes, why and with whom. It is written to be read, not to tick a box.

secciones.html: {titular}, NIF (Spanish tax ID) {nif}, with registered address at {domicilio} (Spain) and reachable at {correo}. He is the author of Andarama, an open-source program (EUPL-1.2), and maintains andarama.com, the hosted instance. The owner's details are also in the legal notice.

To know how many people visit the site we use Plausible, a European service that sets no cookies, stores no IP addresses and does not identify anyone across visits. It counts page views and a few anonymous events (for example, that a tool was used). That is why there is no cookie banner: there is nothing to accept.

Tours published with Andarama carry the same kind of analytics: aggregated visits, scenes and hotspots, without cookies and without IPs.

secciones.titulo: If you arrive from an ad
secciones.html:
When someone reaches andarama.com from a Google ad, the address carries a click identifier (gclid, gbraid or wbraid) and sometimes campaign parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content). Only in that case does a notice appear asking whether you let us tell Google, so we know whether the ad works. Anyone arriving any other way sees no notice.

  • If you say yes, the click identifier, the campaign parameters and the page you landed on are kept in your browser's session storage (cleared when you close the tab) and added to the links to app.andarama.com. If you then start the trial, request a demo or pay for a plan, we record it together with the identifier and report it to Google Ads from our server, with user-data and personalisation consent marked as granted, solely to measure the ad.
  • If you say no, the click identifier is discarded and only the campaign parameters are kept, which say which campaign you came from but do not identify you. Nothing is sent to Google.

We do not install the Google tag or any advertising cookie: everything goes through our server. The legal basis is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time by writing to {correo}. The identifier is used for at most 90 days from the click. Google (Google Ireland Limited) processes what it receives under its own privacy policy.

If you create an account on app.andarama.com, sign-up, sign-in and plan billing are handled by Clerk. Clerk stores your email, your name if you give it, your sign-in method and billing details; to keep you signed in it uses technical cookies, which are essential for the application to work. Tours, media and everything you create are stored in Andarama's own database, not in Clerk. Clerk is a United States company: this data is processed there, with the safeguards for international transfers that Clerk provides in its data processing agreement. Card payments are processed by Stripe through Clerk; Andarama never sees your card number.

andarama.com is served from Cloudflare (Workers, D1, R2 and KV). The database (D1) and the media you upload (R2) are located in Western European data centres. The code runs on Cloudflare's network, in the data centre closest to the visitor, and some short-lived technical data (KV) is replicated across the network. Cloudflare processes requests as a data processor and may keep technical logs for a limited time for security.

These are the companies that process data on behalf of andarama.com:

  • Cloudflare, Inc. (United States; database and media in Western Europe): hosting, database, storage and abuse protection.
  • Clerk, Inc. (United States): accounts, sign-in and plan billing, with Stripe as payment processor.
  • Plausible Insights OÜ (Estonia, European Union): cookie-free visitor analytics.
  • {proveedor_correo} (United States): sending transactional email (account notices and replies to demo requests).

And, only if you accept the ad notice, Google Ireland Limited receives the click identifier and the conversion, as explained above.

The 360 viewer, the little planet maker and the cubemap converter run entirely in your browser. The images you open with them are not uploaded to any server: they never leave your computer. We only record, without identifying you, that the tool was used.

If you request a demo or a proposal from the training, universities or museums forms, we store your name, your institution, your email, your message, the language and the page you wrote from (and, if you accepted the ad notice, the click identifier), in order to reply to you. The legal basis is your own request. It is kept for as long as the conversation lasts and for two years at most. Accounts receive transactional email (verification, invitations, plan notices), never advertising.

secciones.titulo: Your rights and how to delete your account
secciones.html:
You can request access, rectification, erasure, portability, restriction and objection by writing to {correo}.

To delete your account and everything you have created, email us from the account's address. We delete the account in Clerk and the tours, publications and media from Andarama's database and storage, and confirm it by email within 30 days at most. Signing out or removing access from the app's profile does not by itself delete your tours, which is why full deletion is requested by email. Before that, if you like, export what you have made: you can do so at any time as a ZIP or as an .andarama file.

If you believe something is not being done right, you can lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency, AEPD (aepd.es).
If this policy changes, the date is noted here. Last revision: 27 September 2026.

precios.title: Andarama pricing: free for 14 days, then from $20 a month | andarama
precios.description: Andarama pricing: 14-day free trial with no card and plans from $20 a month with 10 tours. Plans to create and to teach, plus invoices in euros for institutions.
precios.h1: Pricing: free for 14 days, then from $20 a month
precios.lead: Start without a card, with the whole editor, virtual reality and export. If you like it, pick the plan that fits; if not, what you have made is still yours and you can export it.

lista: 14 days from when you create your account, no card required
1 tour and 500 MB of media, with the full editor, virtual reality and export
Tours published during the trial carry the “Made with Andarama” badge
Nothing is charged when it ends: what you made is kept and can be exported; to create and upload more, you choose a plan

lista.q: What currency do I pay in?
lista.a: By card, in US dollars (USD): the payment gateway charges in dollars and your bank handles any exchange. Institutions that need an invoice in euros can request one, as explained below.

lista.q: Can I pay by invoice in euros?
lista.a: Yes, if you are a university, a school, a museum, a public body or a company. Write to us and we will send you a quote and an invoice in euros with your tax details, payable by bank transfer; if needed, we submit it through FACe. The details are in procurement for institutions.

lista.q: Do prices include tax?
lista.a: Any applicable indirect taxes (VAT, IGIC or others) depend on your country and on whether you buy as an individual or as a business, and are itemised on the invoice.

lista.q: What happens when the trial ends?
lista.a: Nothing is charged, because the trial asks for no card. What you have created is kept and can be exported; to create more tours and upload more media you need to choose a plan.

lista.q: Does it renew automatically? How do I cancel?
lista.a: Monthly and yearly plans renew automatically at the end of each period. You can cancel whenever you like from your account on app.andarama.com: the plan stays active until the end of the paid period and you are not charged again. De por vida is a one-off payment. It is all in the terms of service.

lista.q: Do I have a right of withdrawal?
lista.a: When you subscribe you ask for the plan to be activated immediately, so, as digital content, the right of withdrawal is lost once it has started (article 103 m of the Spanish consumer protection act, texto refundido de la Ley General para la Defensa de los Consumidores). That is what the 14-day trial with no card is for: you try before you pay.

lista.q: Can I take my tours with me?
lista.a: Yes, on any plan and after the trial too: static ZIP, single HTML file or PWA, which work with no Andarama behind them, and the .andarama file with the project.

lista.q: What if I install it myself?
lista.a: It is free and has no quotas: the same program, open source under EUPL-1.2, on your computer, on Docker or in your Cloudflare account. The open source page explains how.

instituciones.texto: Universities, schools, museums and public bodies: invoice in euros on request, minor contract (Spanish public procurement), security and data protection documentation, and a self-hosted install with support if you prefer.

secciones.titulo: 1. Who provides the service and what these terms cover
secciones.html: The hosted Andarama service (andarama.com and app.andarama.com) is provided by {titular}, NIF (Spanish tax ID) {nif}, with registered address at {domicilio} (Spain) and email {correo}. These terms apply to the use of your account and to subscribing to plans. The Andarama program, when you install it yourself, is governed only by its open-source licence (EUPL-1.2), not by these terms.

You must be at least 14 years old to create an account and have legal capacity to contract to subscribe to a paid plan. Sign-up and sign-in are handled by Clerk. You are responsible for keeping your access safe and for what is done with your account; if you suspect misuse, let us know.

Plans are purchased on app.andarama.com: you choose the plan and billing period, review the price and pay by card through the payment gateway (Clerk, with Stripe as processor). The contract is concluded when the payment is confirmed, and you receive the receipt by email. The contract is concluded in Spanish; translations of these terms are for information only and, in case of any discrepancy, the Spanish version prevails.

Institutions and companies can also purchase with a quote and an invoice in euros: the contract is concluded when they accept the quote or send us the purchase order.

Current prices are on the pricing page. By card they are charged in US dollars (USD); your bank handles the exchange. By invoice, in euros. Any applicable indirect taxes (VAT, IGIC or others) are applied according to the regulations and the customer's location, and are itemised on the invoice. If a price changes, we will notify you by email at least 30 days before the next renewal, and you can cancel before it applies.

When you create your account you get a 14-day trial with no card, with 1 tour and 500 MB of media; what you publish during the trial carries the “Made with Andarama” badge. The trial does not turn into a paid plan on its own. When it ends, what you created is kept and can be exported, and you need a plan to create or upload more.

Monthly and yearly plans renew automatically at the end of each period for the same amount, unless a price change has been notified. You can cancel renewal whenever you like from your account: the plan stays active until the end of the period already paid and you are not charged again. Periods already started are not refunded, except where the law requires it.

The De por vida plan is a one-off payment and lasts for as long as the hosted service at andarama.com is provided. If it ever ceased to be provided, you would be notified at least 90 days in advance so you can export everything or move it to a self-hosted install.

If you are a consumer, you generally have 14 calendar days to withdraw from a distance contract. Andarama plans are digital content not supplied on a tangible medium: when you subscribe you expressly request that the plan be activated immediately and you accept that you therefore lose the right of withdrawal once performance has begun, in accordance with article 103 m) of the Spanish consumer protection act (texto refundido de la Ley General para la Defensa de los Consumidores y Usuarios, Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2007). That is why we offer a 14-day trial with no card first.

If you did not give that consent, or the plan has not yet been activated, you can withdraw within 14 days by writing to {correo} (you can use the model form in annex B of that act, or any clear message), and we will refund the amount within 14 days at most using the same payment method. Companies and institutions are not consumers for these purposes.

You are responsible for what you upload and publish, and for holding the rights to it (photos, texts, audio, video, trademarks and the image of any people who appear). You may not use the service for unlawful content, to infringe the rights of others, to distribute malware or to overload it on purpose. We may remove content or suspend an account that breaks these rules, notifying you unless the seriousness of the case or the law prevents it.

Plans have tour and storage quotas and a fair-use policy: they are meant for one person or a small team. If usage stops looking like that, we talk to you before cutting anything off.

We work to keep the service always available, but there may be interruptions for maintenance, provider failures or causes beyond our control. Unless agreed in writing, there is no guaranteed service level. Support is provided by email.

What you create is yours. You can export your tours at any time and on any plan, also after the trial or after cancelling: static ZIP, single HTML file, PWA and the .andarama file. If you cancel, your tours and media are kept for as long as the account exists; if you request deletion by email, they are erased within 30 days at most, as explained in the privacy policy. For institutions and companies we prepare, on request, the data processing agreement under article 28 of the GDPR.

We are responsible for providing the service with due diligence. Except in cases of wilful misconduct or gross negligence, and except for what the law does not allow to be limited towards consumers, our liability is limited to the amount paid in the twelve months before the event giving rise to it. We recommend keeping the originals of your photographs and exporting your tours from time to time.
If these terms change in a significant way, we will notify you by email at least 30 days in advance. If you do not agree, you can cancel before they take effect.

These terms are governed by Spanish law. If you are a consumer, you may go to the courts of your place of residence; in all other cases, the parties submit to the courts and tribunals of Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Before anything else, write to us: almost everything gets sorted with an email.

seguridad.title: Security and data protection | andarama
seguridad.description: How andarama.com is built: architecture on Cloudflare, where the data lives, encryption, backups, auditable code and exit plan. No certifications we do not have.
seguridad.lead: What the IT department or the data protection officer usually asks before buying, answered with what is actually there.

secciones.html: andarama.com runs on Cloudflare: a Worker serves the API, the Studio and the tours; the database is D1 (managed SQLite); media and tiles are stored in R2 (object storage); KV holds short-lived technical data and Durable Objects coordinate real-time editing and live guided visits. Accounts, sign-in and billing are handled by Clerk. Tour analytics are our own and cookie-free, and website analytics are done by Plausible.

• Database (D1) and media (R2): in Cloudflare data centres in Western Europe. This is the location chosen when they were created; we are working on also pinning it to the European Union jurisdiction.
  • Execution: the code runs on Cloudflare's network, in the data centre closest to the visitor.
  • KV: ephemeral technical data (read sessions, publication pointers) replicated across the network.
  • Accounts and billing: in Clerk, in the United States (email, name, session and billing details). Tours and media do not go through Clerk.
  • Website analytics: Plausible, in the European Union, with no cookies and no IP addresses.

If the institution needs everything to stay in-house, the same application can be installed on its own infrastructure (see below).

All traffic goes over HTTPS with TLS and HSTS. Cloudflare encrypts the D1 database and R2 objects at rest. Passwords and service secrets are never stored in plain text, and API tokens are stored as a hash.

On andarama.com access is managed by Clerk, with two-step verification available. Inside the application, organisations have roles (admin, editor, contributor, reader) and permissions are checked on the server on every route. A self-hosted install also offers local accounts with two-step verification (TOTP) and institutional SSO via OIDC.

Content Security Policy (CSP) with nonces, double-token CSRF protection, rate limits, Turnstile against form abuse, sanitised SVG, Markdown and CSS, and an audit log of administrative actions. Continuous integration runs the tests and the dependency audit on every change.

D1 allows point-in-time recovery of the database (Time Travel) for the period Cloudflare offers, and the admin panel exports a full copy of the database. R2 media has no automatic versioning: that is why we recommend keeping the originals of your photographs and exporting important tours.

The full code is published under EUPL-1.2 on GitHub: anyone can check how data is handled. Vulnerabilities are reported privately following the repository's SECURITY.md file. More on the open source page.

Nothing you create gets locked in. Tours can be exported at any time as a static ZIP, a single HTML file or a PWA, which work without Andarama, and as an .andarama file. The tour.json format is documented. And the same application can be installed on the institution's infrastructure (Docker, its Cloudflare account or a desktop executable), so the day the hosted service is no longer contracted, the work carries on.

Andarama does not hold its own certification under Spain's National Security Framework (ENS) or ISO 27001. Cloudflare and Clerk hold their own certifications as providers. If the institution requires ENS, a self-hosted install on its infrastructure falls under its own ENS. On request we prepare the data processing agreement (article 28 of the GDPR) and a technical sheet with this information.

cta.texto: Data processing agreement, technical sheet, accessibility statement or a meeting with your IT department: ask us and we will send it over.

accesibilidad.title: Accessibility statement | andarama
accesibilidad.description: Accessibility statement for andarama.com, the Andarama viewer and the Studio: partially conformant with WCAG 2.1 AA according to the self-evaluation of 27 September 2026, what was checked, what is missing and how to contact us.
accesibilidad.lead: We want anyone to be able to walk through an Andarama tour, and the institutions that use it to be able to meet their accessibility obligations. This is the real situation.

secciones.html: This statement applies to andarama.com (the public site), to the viewer that displays published tours and to app.andarama.com (the Studio, the editor). We take as reference Spain's Real Decreto 1112/2018 on the accessibility of public sector websites and the UNE-EN 301 549 standard, which refers to the WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines.

Partially conformant with WCAG 2.1 level AA. On the screens evaluated there is no serious or critical failure left that can be detected automatically, and what was checked by hand with the keyboard works, but some aspects have not been checked and there are exceptions, listed below. This is a self-evaluation: no external audit and no testing with screen reader users have been carried out yet.

Evaluation of 27 September 2026, with two methods:

  • Automated, with axe-core and the WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 level A and AA rules. It is part of the end-to-end tests, runs on every code change and fails on any serious or critical failure. An automated tool only detects part of the possible problems.
  • Manual, with the keyboard: going through with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and Escape to check the focus order, that focus is visible, that dialogs keep focus and give it back when closed, and that content reflows at 640 pixels wide (the same as 200% zoom on a 1280 screen).

Screens evaluated: on andarama.com, the home page, pricing, training, classroom, the blog, one of its posts and this statement; in the viewer, a published tour with its scene, a hotspot panel, help, the share dialog and the accessible version; in the Studio, sign-in, projects, the media library, the plan page, the editor (scenes and properties, graph, settings, translations, versions and comments) and the publish, export and share dialogs.

secciones.titulo: What has been checked to conform
secciones.html:
• No serious or critical axe failures on the screens evaluated.
  • The language of every page is declared in the document, including the viewer and the Studio.
  • Viewer: hotspots can be reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space; panels and dialogs (help, share, final screen, quiz result) keep focus, close with Escape and return focus to the button that opened them; the closed scene menu is out of the tab order.
  • Visible focus on every control checked.
  • The reduced-motion preference (prefers-reduced-motion) is respected: neither panels nor the menu are animated.
  • At 640 pixels wide the site does not require horizontal scrolling and the viewer toolbar folds behind a button that unfolds it again.
  • Linear accessible version of the tour, scene changes announced to screen readers and WebVTT subtitles on 360 video and on video hotspots.
  • Studio: a “Skip to content” link, dialogs that keep focus and close with Escape, and text with a contrast of at least 4.5:1 on the screens evaluated.

secciones.titulo: What is not accessible or has not been checked
secciones.html:
• Exploring a 360 photo is visual by nature: the alternative is the linear accessible version, whose quality depends on the texts written by whoever creates the tour.
  • Alternative text is only required if the publisher turns on “Require alternative text to publish” in the tour settings; otherwise a tour can be published without it.
  • Some Studio operations are designed for a mouse or touch screen (placing a hotspot by clicking on the panorama, arranging the graph or the floor plan by dragging) and it has not been checked that all of them have an equivalent keyboard alternative.
  • It has not yet been tested with screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS) or with people with disabilities.
  • The plans page and payment in the hosted version use forms from an external provider that are not covered by the automated test.
  • Embedded third-party content (web pages, YouTube or Vimeo videos, 3D models) depends on its source.
  • A tour’s custom themes and colours may not reach the minimum contrast.
  • Virtual reality with a headset has no equivalent alternative inside the immersive session.

secciones.titulo: If you publish tours for a public institution
secciones.html:
Each body is responsible for the accessibility of what it publishes. To make a tour as accessible as possible: write alternative text for every scene and every image, give hotspots text, subtitle videos and check the contrast if you change the colours. This statement serves as supplier information for your own.

If your organisation needs it, turn on “Require alternative text to publish” in the tour settings: the Studio will not publish while any scene or hotspot lacks alternative text.
If you find an accessibility barrier, or need content in an accessible format, write to us at {correo}. We reply within 20 working days at most.

Statement prepared on 27 September 2026 through a self-evaluation by our own team (automated testing with axe and manual keyboard review). Last reviewed: 27 September 2026. It will be reviewed after the external audit and, in any case, every year.

codigoAbierto.title: Open source: EUPL-1.2, self-hosting and repository | andarama
codigoAbierto.description: Andarama is open source under EUPL-1.2: you can read it, audit it, install it on your server and modify it. What is in the repository and what happens if Andarama shuts down.
codigoAbierto.lead: Andarama is not a cut-down version with a cloud behind it: the andarama.com service and what you install yourself are the same program, published in full.

secciones.html: Andarama is published under the European Union Public Licence (EUPL) 1.2, the European Commission's licence, with an official version in every EU language. It allows you to use, study, modify and redistribute the program, including for commercial purposes. Anyone who distributes a modified version, or offers it as a network service, must publish their changes under the same licence (or a compatible one).

Everything is at github.com/joseluissaorin/andarama: the API, the Studio, the viewer, the exporter, the panorama tiler, the data schema, the documentation and the deployments. Strict TypeScript, unit and end-to-end tests, and continuous integration with dependency audits. Issues and proposals are opened there.

Three ways, the same program and no quotas:

  • Desktop: an executable for macOS, Windows and Linux, with a double click (guide).
  • Docker: Node and SQLite in one image, with one volume and one port (guide).
  • Cloudflare: your own account, with one command that creates the resources and migrates the database (guide).

A self-hosted install has no plans and no limits other than those set by whoever runs it, and can use local accounts with two-step verification or institutional SSO via OIDC.

secciones.titulo: A format that does not expire
secciones.html: Tours are stored in tour.json, a documented and versioned format (reference). Exports (static ZIP, single HTML file, PWA) work with no Andarama behind them, on any hosting or from a USB stick.

It is the question that decides a public purchase, and it has an answer: the code would remain published and anyone could keep using, installing and maintaining it; exported tours would keep working, and the hosted service would give notice in good time so you can take everything with you. Nobody depends on us still being here.

The andarama.com service adds what running a server requires: hosting, backups, updates, accounts with Clerk and the plans. If you would rather not maintain anything, it is there; if you would rather have it on your own infrastructure, that works too. For institutions we offer a self-hosted install with support: see procurement.

cta.titulo: Shall we install it on your premises?
cta.texto: If your institution prefers to keep it on its own infrastructure, we deploy it with you and you contract support and updates.

No certifications we do not have: Andarama does not hold its own ENS (Spain's National Security Framework) certification; if the institution requires it, a self-hosted install falls under its own ENS.
If you want to close the purchase within the financial year, write to us in good time: we prepare the quote within one or two working days and the invoice as soon as we receive the purchase order.

bloques.titulo: From camera to listing in an afternoon
bloques.texto: Take the 360 photos with an Insta360, a Ricoh Theta or any camera that produces equirectangular images. Upload them all at once: the importer sorts them and tiles them in your browser. Drag one room onto another to create the step, publish and paste the link wherever you like.
The Paseo plan is $20 a month (or $200 a year) with 10 tours at a time: about $2 a month per listing. When one sells, you unpublish it and reuse the slot for the next. No per-view or per-photo fees.

bloques.titulo: On your agency website and on the listing
bloques.texto: Every tour has its own link, a QR code for the office window and an iframe or a script line to embed it on the property page. It works on phones with the gyroscope and on VR headsets with nothing to install.
With the Excursión plan ($500 a year, up to 500 tours) tours go out without the Andarama badge and under your agency's domain.
A floor plan showing where each room is, text with square footage and finishes, detail photos, video and a contact form inside the tour itself.

Andarama works with 360 photographs: it does not do LiDAR scans, 3D dollhouse views or measured floor plans like Matterport. If you need that, Matterport is still the option; if you need to show a home well at a low cost, this is enough.

lista.q: Which camera do I need?
lista.a: Any that takes 2:1 equirectangular photos: Insta360 X3 or X4, Ricoh Theta, Kandao, GoPro Max… or a phone with a panorama app. There is no proprietary camera and no hardware rental.

lista.q: Can I have more than 10 listings?
lista.a: Yes: the Excursión plan allows up to 500 tours for $500 a year, with no badge and your own domain.

lista.q: Can I add the tours to MLS listings and property portals?
lista.a: MLS listings and property portals usually have a field for a virtual tour link; the Andarama link works there. On your agency website it embeds with an iframe or the WordPress plugin.

lista.q: What happens if I stop paying?
lista.a: You can export any tour as a static ZIP and host it wherever you like, with no Andarama behind it.

visor.title: Free 360 photo viewer online: view 360 photos in your browser | andarama
visor.description: Free online 360 photo viewer. Open an equirectangular photo (JPG or PNG) and look around in 360 with fullscreen and VR, without uploading anything to any server.
visor.h1: 360 photo viewer online: view your equirectangular photo in the browser
visor.lead: Pick a 360 photo and it appears right here as if you were wearing a headset: drag to look around, scroll to zoom, fullscreen and virtual reality if your browser has WebXR. Nothing is uploaded: the viewer is Andarama's own engine running on your computer.
visor.rv_no: This browser has no WebXR. Open this same page from the browser of a Meta Quest, Pico or Vision Pro headset.
visor.cuerpo:
What a 360 photo is and why it looks wrong in a normal viewer

A 360 (equirectangular) photo is a sphere unrolled onto a 2:1 rectangle: the 360 degrees of turn along the width and the 180 degrees from top to bottom along the height. Opened in an ordinary photo viewer it looks stretched, with the floor and the sky distorted and straight lines bent into curves. A 360 viewer wraps the image back onto a sphere and puts you at the centre, so you look around as if you were there.

How to use this online 360 viewer

  1. Press “Choose a 360 photo” or drop the file onto the dotted area. It takes the JPG and PNG files produced by Insta360, Ricoh Theta, GoPro Max, Kandao, phone panorama apps or any stitching software.
  2. Drag with the mouse or a finger to turn; use the wheel or pinch to zoom in and out; with the keyboard, the arrow keys.
  3. The fullscreen button fills the monitor; the headset button starts a virtual reality session if the browser has WebXR (Meta Quest, Pico, Vision Pro with Safari or a PC with a headset).

Nothing gets uploaded

The image never travels to a server: the browser decodes it and the WebGL engine paints it on your graphics card. You can use it with private or client photos without them leaving your computer. And since there is no upload, there is no waiting either: an 8K photo opens in a couple of seconds.

View 360 photos on PC, phone and headset

This viewer works in any modern browser: Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge, on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. On a phone you can turn the view with the gyroscope. On a VR headset, the same page offers the enter-VR button and the photo wraps the whole room.

What it doesn't do (and where to do it)

It doesn't store the photo or generate a link to share it: that would require uploading it somewhere. If you want to share a 360 photo by link, embed it on your website, connect several into a tour or add hotspots, that is what Andarama does, and you can try it free for fourteen days.

faq.q: Which formats does the viewer accept?
faq.a: Equirectangular JPG and PNG files with a 2:1 ratio, which is what every 360 camera and stitching program produces. It also opens panoramas that don't cover the full 360 degrees, though there will be a black band.
The limit is your browser's memory. 8K photos (8192×4096) open without trouble on any computer; above 16K the image is reduced automatically so the graphics card can handle it.

faq.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything happens in your browser: the photo is read from disk, decoded and drawn with WebGL. We only record, without identifying you, that the tool was used.

faq.q: Can I view the photo with a VR headset?
faq.a: Yes, if the browser has WebXR: open this page from the browser of a Meta Quest, Pico or Vision Pro and press the headset button. On a phone without WebXR you can turn the view with the gyroscope.

faq.q: How do I share a 360 photo by link?
faq.a: This viewer doesn't store it. To get a link, embed it on a website or connect several photos into a tour, create an account on Andarama: the trial lasts fourteen days and asks for no card.

planeta.title: Little planet maker online, free | andarama
planeta.description: Turn a 360 photo into a little planet (tiny planet) and download it as PNG. Free, in the browser, without uploading the image anywhere.
planeta.h1: Little planet maker: turn your 360 photo into a tiny planet
planeta.lead: Upload an equirectangular photo and out comes the planet: the ground at the centre, the sky all around. Rotate it, open or close the world and download it as PNG at whatever size you like. All in your browser.
planeta.cuerpo:
What a little planet is

A little planet (or tiny planet) is a stereographic projection of a 360 photo: take the whole sphere, rest it on the ground and project it onto a plane from the zenith. The result is a disc with the ground at the centre, buildings and trees growing outwards and the sky wrapping around the edge. It is the most photogenic way to show, in a single image, everything that surrounded the camera.

How to make a little planet with this tool

  1. Choose an equirectangular photo (2:1 JPG or PNG) from any 360 camera or panorama app.
  2. Adjust the rotation to decide what ends up at the top of the planet and the opening to bring the horizon closer or further away. The planet is recalculated instantly.
  3. Pick the output size and the background (transparent to compose it over something else) and download the PNG.

Tips for a good planet

Photos with a clean nadir (no tripod, no hand) work best, because the centre of the disc is precisely the ground. Scenes with an open horizon and an interesting sky make the nicest planets; squares, courtyards and summits are winning cases. If the original is tilted, fix it first: the projection exaggerates any lean.

No upload, no watermark

The calculation runs pixel by pixel in your browser with the same routine Andarama's media library uses to show its thumbnails. The photo never leaves your computer and the PNG you download is yours, with no watermark and no resolution limit beyond your machine's memory.

faq.a: Anything between 512 and 4096 pixels per side. Final sharpness depends on the original photo: an 8K equirectangular gives perfectly crisp 4096 px planets.
Yes: download at 2048 or 4096 px with a white or black background and upload it as a square image. The transparent background is handy for compositing over another design.

faq.q: Can I make the planet inside out (sky at the centre)?
faq.a: Not yet from this tool. That is the “tunnel” projection; if you would like it, write to us and we will add it.
No. It is computed in your browser and never travels to any server.

cubemap.title: Equirectangular to cubemap converter online (and back) | andarama
cubemap.description: Free equirectangular panorama to cubemap converter: six PNG faces or a ZIP, and cubemap to equirectangular. In the browser, nothing uploaded.
cubemap.h1: Equirectangular to cubemap (and cubemap to equirectangular)
cubemap.lead: Upload a 2:1 panorama and get the six cube faces as PNG, separately or in a ZIP. Or the other way round: pick six faces and an equirectangular gets stitched. Everything is computed in your browser.
cubemap.cuerpo:
What a cubemap is and what it is for

A cubemap represents the surroundings with six square images, one per face of a cube: front, back, left, right, up and down. It is the format expected by 3D engines (Unity, Unreal, Godot, Three.js, Babylon), game skyboxes, reflection maps and many 360 viewers, because each face is a normal texture without the equirectangular's distortion at the poles.

How to convert an equirectangular to a cubemap

  1. Choose the equirectangular panorama (2:1 JPG or PNG).
  2. Pick the face size. The rule is the panorama's width divided by four: an 8192 px equirectangular gives 2048 px faces.
  3. Download the six faces separately or as a ZIP named f, b, l, r, u, d (the Marzipano and krpano convention) or with your engine's naming.

And from cubemap to equirectangular

The reverse path is here too: choose the six faces and the tool stitches them into a single 2:1 panorama ready for any 360 viewer, for social media or for Andarama. Useful to recover a game skybox, a Blender render in cube format or a panorama from a camera that exports faces.

How it is computed

For every pixel of every face, a direction is traced from the centre of the cube, converted to longitude and latitude, and the matching point of the equirectangular is read. It is the same geometry Andarama's tiler uses to prepare tours, executed here on a Canvas inside your browser. No image is uploaded anywhere.

faq.q: Which face size should I choose?
faq.a: The equirectangular's width divided by four: 4096 wide, 1024 px faces; 8192, 2048 px faces. A larger size adds no detail, only weight.

faq.q: In which order and with which names do the faces come out?
faq.a: By default with the Marzipano and krpano convention (f, b, l, r, u, d). You can also pick the Unity and Three.js one (px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz).
No, images only. For 360 video you need a desktop program such as FFmpeg with the v360 filter.
